title: Usage insights: add route/model aggregate tables + materialized views (hourly/daily) and backfill job
author: Mei Lin
description: Summary: This PR introduces the first set of persisted aggregates for in-console “usage insights” (cost + perf) broken down by route and model. It adds ClickHouse tables + materialized views for hourly and daily rollups, plus an idempotent backfill/recompute job to populate historical partitions once route/model dimensions land in metering. This is the backing store for the upcoming /insights/routes list + route detail endpoints (ENG-8423/8424). What’s included: 1) New aggregate tables (ClickHouse): - usage_insights_route_model_hourly (window_start at hour) - usage_insights_route_model_daily (window_start at day) Both tables are scoped by tenant boundaries and core filters: org_id, project_id, env, region, deployment_mode, route_norm, route_hash, model, model_variant (nullable), plus cost/perf measures. 2) Materialized views: - mv_metering_to_usage_insights_route_model_hourly - mv_metering_to_usage_insights_route_model_daily These consume metering events from metering_events_v3 (post-route plumbing) and incrementally update aggregates. 3) Partitioning + ordering strategy: - PARTITION BY toYYYYMMDD(window_start) for hourly and toYYYYMM(window_start) for daily - ORDER BY (org_id, project_id, env, region, deployment_mode, window_start, route_hash, model) - route_norm is stored for display; route_hash used as primary key-like join dimension to control index size and mitigate long strings. 4) Backfill/recompute job: tools/usage_insights/backfill_route_model_aggregates.py (invoked via internal jobs runner) - Supports --from/--to time windows (aligned to hour/day boundaries) - Loads source events from metering_events_v3, replays into aggregates using INSERT SELECT with deterministic grouping - Uses “replace partition” mode to keep job idempotent: for each partition, we write to a temp table and EXCHANGE PARTITION into the target (safer than in-place mutations under load). - Includes guardrails: max window (default 7 days), concurrency cap, and dry-run query planner output. 5) Metrics and correctness checks (minimal): - Adds a small set of statsd counters: backfill.partitions_processed, backfill.rows_written, backfill.failed_partitions - Adds a validation query script that compares aggregate totals vs raw metering totals for a sampled set of org/project pairs. Schema notes / metrics captured: - Cost measures: total_cost_usd, input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens, cached_output_tokens, unit_cost_usd_per_1k_tokens (computed at query time), gpu_ms_proxy (nullable; populated when metering_event includes it) - Perf measures: request_count, error_count, latency_ms_p50, latency_ms_p95 (p50/p95 computed via ClickHouse quantileState aggregation; merged at query time via quantileMerge) - Dimensions: route_norm (normalized, length-limited string), route_hash (sha256 hex prefix), model (catalog name), model_variant (optional, e.g., “q4_k_m”, “fp16”), plus org/project/env/region/deployment_mode. Cardinality controls (tie-in to standards): - route_norm is normalized upstream per ADR but we also defensively enforce: trim, lowercase, maxlen=120, allowed charset filter. If normalization fails or route is missing, route_norm becomes “unknown” and route_hash is hash('unknown'). - For obviously dynamic routes (contains >2 numeric segments or UUID-like patterns), we set route_norm to “other” and add a boolean is_route_rolled_up=1. This logic is intentionally conservative; we can tune once we see real traffic. (Thomas: please sanity check the heuristics; they’re in route_normalize.py). Query examples (used by ENG-8423/8424): - Top routes by cost for a time range (hourly): SELECT route_norm, sum(total_cost_usd) AS cost_usd, sum(request_count) AS reqs, quantileMerge(0.95)(latency_ms_p95_state) AS p95 FROM usage_insights_route_model_hourly WHERE org_id=? AND project_id=? AND env=? AND window_start >= ? AND window_start < ? GROUP BY route_norm ORDER BY cost_usd DESC LIMIT 100; - Route detail: breakdown by model: SELECT model, sum(total_cost_usd) AS cost_usd, sum(input_tokens) AS in_tok, sum(output_tokens) AS out_tok FROM usage_insights_route_model_hourly WHERE ... AND route_hash=? GROUP BY model ORDER BY cost_usd DESC; Rollout plan: - Land tables/MVs behind feature flag ENABLE_USAGE_INSIGHTS_AGGREGATES=1 in the jobs deployment; by default, MVs are created but set to “stopped” (see migrations below) until we enable ingestion in staging. - Backfill will be run in staging for the last 14 days, then prod for the last 7 days initially (to validate performance). We can extend once we confirm cardinality and storage growth. Files / areas changed (high level): - db/migrations/clickhouse/2026_02_06_usage_insights_route_model_hourly.sql - db/migrations/clickhouse/2026_02_06_usage_insights_route_model_daily.sql - db/migrations/clickhouse/2026_02_06_mv_metering_to_usage_insights_route_model_*.sql - services/telemetry-aggregator/src/route_normalize.py - services/telemetry-aggregator/src/materialized_views.py (registration + enable/disable) - tools/usage_insights/backfill_route_model_aggregates.py - tools/usage_insights/validate_route_model_aggregates.sql - docs/internal/usage_insights/aggregates.md (operator notes: retention, partitions, job flags) Commits: - 9f3b0db Add hourly/daily aggregate schemas for usage insights route/model - 2a7c1e6 Wire up materialized views from metering_events_v3 (quantileState for latency) - 6c2d9a1 Add route normalization + rollup heuristics (defensive) - 0f414f8 Add backfill/recompute job with EXCHANGE PARTITION strategy - 5e8f4c0 Add validation queries + operator docs Testing: - Unit tests: route normalization (uuid detection, long route truncation, missing route -> unknown) - Integration: local ClickHouse container run for migrations + MV insert smoke test - Load sanity: replayed ~25M metering rows (synthetic) into hourly aggregates; ~2.8s/partition on dev laptop w/ container (see notes below). Perf / storage notes: - Hourly table uses quantileState columns; expect slightly higher storage but enables accurate p95 merges across groupings. - Daily table stores quantileState as well; we can decide later if daily should store only sums to reduce footprint. Open questions (not blocking): - Whether we need a weekly rollup table for long time ranges (API will likely cap to 30d for now). - Whether to include ‘sdk’ as a dimension for debugging (out of scope per PM). Review notes / discussion highlights: - Nadia asked to ensure cached tokens are additive and not double-counted across fallback model events; this PR assumes upstream metering emits one event per request with cached tokens split out. If upstream changes to multi-event per request, we’ll need to group by request_id (not done here). - Allison requested keeping MV stop/start toggles for incident response; added enable_mv flag and documented rollback steps. - Thomas requested we avoid storing full route_norm in ORDER BY; we now order by route_hash and keep route_norm as a display field. CI: - Build: pass - Unit tests: pass - Lint: pass - ClickHouse migration check: pass - Container integration tests: pass Merge: Squash merged into main. Follow-ups: - ENG-8423 will add query-side LIMIT/offset + “other” bucket behavior; this PR only provides storage primitives. - ENG-8429 will operationalize backfill scheduling + runbook; for now, operator docs are in docs/internal/usage_insights/aggregates.md.

conversation: Logan Wright (review): Overall looks good. Two asks: (1) please document the MV stop/start mechanism and (2) confirm ORDER BY doesn’t include the full route string (we’ve had index bloat before).

Mei Lin (author): Added docs/internal/usage_insights/aggregates.md with MV enable/disable + rollback steps. Also changed ORDER BY to use route_hash instead of route_norm; route_norm stays as display-only.
Thomas Baird (review): The dynamic route rollup heuristic worries me. Can you add tests for UUIDs + numeric IDs and make sure we don’t roll up common versioned endpoints (e.g., /v1/chat/completions)?
Mei Lin (author): Added test vectors for UUID-like segments and numeric segments. Version prefixes (/v1, /v2) are explicitly excluded from rollup detection.

Nadia Rahman (review): Quantiles: good call on quantileState, but please ensure you’re using quantileTiming for latency (ms) rather than quantileExact. Also, are cached tokens always present? Some sources only emit cached_input_tokens.
Mei Lin (author): Switched to quantileTimingState for latency_ms. For tokens, columns are nullable w/ default 0 at insert time; missing cached_output_tokens will stay 0.
Allison Grant (review): For SRE purposes, I want a way to quickly stop the MV ingestion if we see runaway cardinality. Is that behind a flag or do we need to drop MVs?

Mei Lin (author): Added ENABLE_USAGE_INSIGHTS_AGGREGATES gate in telemetry-aggregator (MV creation remains, but ingestion is stopped by default). Also documented manual STOP VIEW commands in operator docs.
Chloe Martin (review): Can you add an example query that matches what the route list endpoint will do (top 100 routes by spend, filtered by env/region)? Helps validate groupings.
Mei Lin (author): Added query examples in PR description + in aggregates.md.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved after the ORDER BY change + docs. Let’s keep backfill windows small initially in prod.
Nadia Rahman (approval): Approved. Please coordinate with ENG-8435 if metering schema changes to multiple events per request.
Thomas Baird (approval): Approved with tests added. We should revisit heuristics once we see beta traffic.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Flag + STOP VIEW docs cover my needs.
